effect_mechanism: Putting tree cover back on cleared or degraded land rebuilds the structure that forest species need, and then lets dispersers do the rest. Measured against degraded ecosystems across 221 study landscapes worldwide, forest restoration enhanced biodiversity by 15-84% and vegetation structure by 36-77% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1]. How the cover is re-established changes the result: natural regeneration surpassed active restoration for plants, birds and invertebrates, with restoration success 34 to 56% higher after controlling for forest cover, precipitation and time [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1]. Recovery is a function of time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], and the clock is slow — a secondary Atlantic forest was estimated to need 65 years, with a range of 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. What accelerates it is anything that brings seed in or keeps grazing out: beneath framework-species plantings, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]; artificial perches brought native zoochoric regeneration that was absent from the planted rings [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_2]; and Senegalese exclosures carried 27 woody species after a year against 51 in the 5- and 12-year enclosures, more than 52% higher richness [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1]. Practitioners implementing these technologies in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, India, Niger and Turkmenistan record plant, animal and habitat diversity rising as cover returns and protection holds [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The other route is keeping the forest that exists, since the governance instruments that retain cover also hold the habitat: GEF sustainable forest management sites lost about 0.27% less forest each year than matched areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], payments improved forest cover and reduced deforestation in pooled analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2], and participatory management is credited with regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2]. A global analysis of community forests found environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1].
conditionality: This is a landscape benefit rather than an on-farm one: the biodiversity gain accrues to the restored forest and the landscape around it, not to the adopting farmer's fields. The class follows the sub-practice vote, which tempers the pooled result. Natural regeneration and the cross-practice meta-analysis hold the strongest results [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles16_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1]. conditionality: The payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas, which limits what they deliver for biodiversity [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. effect_mechanism: In these upper-middle-income settings the evidence is about succession on land that has been cleared or degraded, and about what speeds it up. Tree species richness rose as a function of time since disturbance across an Atlantic rainforest chronosequence [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1], with a forest estimated to need 65 years, range 23 to 178, to reach a proportion of 80% animal-dispersed species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2]. Assisted recruitment shortens the wait: beneath framework-species plantings in Thai dry forest, tree seedlings of many species recruited, 25 of them animal-dispersed and 11 wind-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and artificial perches produced native zoochoric regenerants that were absent from planted rings, so bringing in dispersers mattered more than the planting itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1]. On Turkmen barkhan sands the revegetated area is recorded as providing habitat for 25-27 species of plants and animals, with plant and animal diversity rated as increasing [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. Holding the cover is the companion mechanism: under community forest management in the Sierra Norte de Puebla, forest cover did not decline after the handover but increased by 8% [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1].
conditionality: The direction is consistent, but the base is thin and soft: chronosequences and site studies, a set of compiler ratings, and a forest-cover change read from land-use maps as a proxy for habitat rather than a count of species [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Where a project was independently evaluated the result was less flattering — biodiversity is hard to assess, the management-effectiveness tool used was not a suitable proxy, and there was no clear-cut evidence that a Vietnamese special-use forest project had a positive impact [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1]. Harm is recorded once: a review reports that China's Grain-for-Green programme rapidly increased tree cover to restore degraded agricultural soils, but used mainly fast-growing non-native species and resulted in a decrease of 6% in native forest cover as farming was displaced to new areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_seddon21_11], a leakage of clearing out of the restored area that a site-level count would miss. Time is the binding condition: the Atlantic-forest estimate spans decades to well over a century before the assemblage approaches the composition of a mature forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2], so nothing here promises a measurable result inside a project cycle. Two reading rules apply. The gains are measured against the degraded or cleared starting point, not against intact forest, and a young stand holding less than old-growth is incomplete recovery rather than loss. And the perch and framework-species findings are about assisting dispersal into a restoration site [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]: they presuppose a seed source within reach, which is a siting condition a scan can test and a restoration in a cleared landscape may fail.

Harm is recorded once: a review reports that China's Grain-for-Green programme rapidly increased tree cover to restore degraded agricultural soils, but used mainly fast-growing non-native species and resulted in a decrease of 6% in native forest cover as farming was displaced to new areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_seddon21_11], a leakage of clearing out of the restored area that a site-level count would miss. Time is the binding condition: the Atlantic-forest estimate spans decades to well over a century before the assemblage approaches the composition of a mature forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_2], so nothing here promises a measurable result inside a project cycle. Two reading rules apply. The gains are measured against the degraded or cleared starting point, not against intact forest, and a young stand holding less than old-growth is incomplete recovery rather than loss. And the perch and framework-species findings are about assisting dispersal into a restoration site [ev_biodiversity_outcome_loureiro21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1]: they presuppose a seed source within reach, which is a siting condition a scan can test and a restoration in a cleared landscape may fail.

effect_mechanism: Both directions are reported. On the gain side, planted stands create habitat and attract seed dispersers: beneath framework-species plantings in northern Thailand thirty-six tree seedling species recruited naturally, 25 of them animal-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and WOCAT compilers rate dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan as raising plant, habitat and animal diversity, citing snakes, lizards and turtles [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. On the loss side, a pantropical review warns that where forests can regenerate naturally or with some assistance, tree planting can reduce biodiversity conservation benefits if the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]. A review of nature-based solutions adds that research in north-west India shows afforestation activities, although they can lead to an aggregate increase in forest cover, in most cases result in loss of diversity and promote monocultures [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_4], and that China's Grain-for-Green programme, which used mainly fast-growing non-native species, resulted in a decrease of 6% in native forest cover as farming was displaced to new areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_seddon21_11].
conditionality: What separates the gain side from the loss side is what the land would do without planting. The cautions apply where forests can regenerate naturally [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1] and where planting is done with few, fast-growing or non-native species, so that cover rises while diversity falls or clearing moves elsewhere [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_4, ev_landscape_forest_cover_seddon21_11]; the gains are on bare dunes and degraded tropical land with no unplanted control [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity]. The actionable reading is a siting and design choice: planting looks favourable where nothing would regenerate otherwise, and risky where natural regeneration is possible or where the planting is a monoculture, unless the species and management provide habitat. Both sides remain thin. The loss side is review sentences carrying the findings of the studies they cite, not measured comparisons of their own; the gain side is compiler ratings and a case study without a control. The plantation-versus-natural-regeneration comparisons that used to weigh on the loss side have moved to the plantation family's biodiversity row.

effect_mechanism: Natural regeneration rebuilds biodiversity as secondary forest develops. Across tropical chronosequences species richness recovers fastest and composition slowest, with richness after 20 years at 78% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_2]; tree species richness in Brazil's Atlantic Forest rises with time since disturbance [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_1]; and in the western Andes of Colombia bird and dung beetle communities in regenerating forest came to resemble old growth [ev_biodiversity_outcome_chazdon16_1]. A pantropical meta-analysis finds natural regeneration outperforms active planting for plants, birds and invertebrates [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], an Ethiopian WOCAT compiler rates animal diversity as increased under area closure [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity], and in Senegal's southern Groundnut Basin woody species richness in exclosures rose from 27 species after 1 year to 51 species after 5 and 12 years, an increase of more than 52% [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].
conditionality: Recovery of composition and endemism is slow: composition after 20 years was only 33% of old-growth values [ev_biodiversity_outcome_poorter21_1], and in the Brazilian Atlantic Forest regaining mature-forest endemism was estimated to take 1987 years [ev_biodiversity_outcome_liebsch08_3]. The meta-analysis compares regeneration with planting rather than with degraded land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_crouzeilles17_1], and the Ethiopian compiler notes that returning wildlife damages crops and livestock [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1414_2011_animal_diversity]. The Senegal result compares exclosures of different ages at one site rather than exclosures with open grazed land [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badji13_1].

effect_mechanism: Most units that set the class point toward loss. An INRAE expert synthesis's own small meta-analysis of species richness in plantations against natural regeneration of the stand after regeneration cutting gives -0.24, a very imprecise estimate from a very small number of cases, with an interval that spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. A review of nature-based solutions states that if non-native tree plantations replace intact native ecosystems such as ancient grasslands, peatlands or woodlands, the outcomes for biodiversity will be poor [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_1]. On the Orissa coast of India, extensive Casuarina plantations established as a storm protection measure caused destruction to olive ridley sea turtle nesting beaches [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badola05_12]. The same review allows a gain in a narrower case: establishing plantations of non-native trees in a highly degraded landscape might benefit biodiversity locally if the trees enable native vegetation to regenerate, or regionally if plantations take pressure off native biodiverse forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_2]. Further INRAE statements point toward loss — plantations generally lead to decreases in biodiversity, or at least to changes in composition at the expense of native species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6], and a cited 40% loss of local species richness in forest plantations relative to uncut control forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2].
conditionality: What separates the loss and the gain is what the plantation replaces: intact native ecosystems or a nesting beach on the loss side [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_badola05_12], a highly degraded landscape where the trees help native vegetation return on the gain side [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_2]. The review units carry findings from the studies they cite, the Casuarina unit is a cited case statement, and the INRAE estimate is non-significant, so none is a demonstrated loss measured against the land a plantation replaced. The declines against uncut or near-natural forest are held out of the class because their comparator is reference forest, not the starting point of a restoration project, so they describe a shortfall from a natural baseline rather than a restoration effect [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6]. The INRAE evidence is temperate and boreal, and only the Indian coastal case comes from the low- and lower-middle-income target. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Protection and community forest management retain and expand forest habitat. GEF sustainable forest management projects show less deforestation than matched areas without projects [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], and forest cover increased by 8% under community management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. A global analysis of community forests found environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate plant and animal diversity as increased under protection [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
conditionality: Most units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction, a component proxy for biodiversity, and the Mexican figure is a before-after comparison with no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. Governance effects are uneven: in the global community-forest analysis environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]; under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
justification.conditionality: Most units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction, a component proxy for biodiversity, and the Mexican figure is a before-after comparison with no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. Governance effects are uneven: in the global community-forest analysis environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]; under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. effect_mechanism: Across the restoration families taken together, carbon gains are real but uneven between families; they accrue in two pools: biomass as the trees grow, and soil organic carbon after the land-use transition. On biomass, natural regeneration removed 9.1 to 18.8 t CO2 per hectare per year during the first 20 years of growth [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_3]. Stock estimates line up with those rates: a 20-year-old secondary natural forest in the moist tropical biome was estimated at 51 t of aboveground carbon per hectare [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch19_1], the median present value of 30-year accumulation from natural regeneration is 60.2 tC per hectare in above- and belowground biomass and soil [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_1], and regeneration over 215 Mha could sequester 23.4 Gt of carbon in aboveground biomass over 30 years [ev_carbon_sequestration_williams24_1]. Measured plantings show the accumulation directly: native-species restoration on former pasture held 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 t C per hectare at three, five and seven years [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_2, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3], and intervention sites were sequestering approximately 1.33 tons of carbon per hectare per year more than without the project [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. On soils, across 151 transitions to forest the average carbon gain was 0.447% of pre-transition soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_1], and practitioners across Niger, India, Tunisia, Bangladesh and Eritrea rate soil organic matter and above-ground biomass as rising under these technologies [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_2325_2017_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1568_2013_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4372_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1330_2010_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C]. A review of nature-based solutions adds that afforestation increases topsoil carbon in carbon-poor soils [ev_soil_organic_carbon_seddon21_5]. Avoided loss carries the rest: keeping existing cover through community management, payments and project support is counted here as retained carbon [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2], and environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it in a global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1].
conditionality: The biomass figures are growth rates over the first decades, not a permanent stock. A young restoration is also far from the reference it is growing towards — the same Atlantic-forest study that measured 21.85 to 38.29 t C per hectare in plantings aged three to seven years measured 138.94 in the mature forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3] — which is incomplete recovery against intact forest, while the gain being claimed is against the pasture the planting replaced. Delivery is not guaranteed by the instrument: a REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], crown-cover gains in broadleaf forests under community management were insignificant [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], of 1,924 assessed project locations 33 showed strong evidence of negative outcomes and 169 no evidence of a positive one [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], and environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]. How much soil carbon is gained by land-use history, climate zone or soil type is not resolved in this row. effect_mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it in a global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases in the global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. justification.mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it in a global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
justification.conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases in the global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

effect_mechanism: This row asks how much water leaves the catchment after forest cover is restored or expanded, and the evidence finds both less and more, with more weight on less. Measured syntheses mostly find less: in about 80% of study cases reporting annual water yields the effect of forest restoration and other forms of forest cover expansion was negative, and in 6% positive [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1]; baseflow decreased in 63% of cases [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2]; groundwater levels or recharge decreased with forest cover expansion in 67% of the studies reporting them [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1]; and no study in the meta-analysis subset showed a water-yield gain [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]. A global review found a significant negative relationship between forest cover gain and annual runoff in large watersheds [ev_water_yield_zhang17_3]. The reason given is interception and use: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, and much of the water that soaks in is used by the trees [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. An FAO synthesis states that the effects of reforestation or afforestation on water yields are usually the reverse of those for forest removal, that low flows are usually diminished as well, especially where fast-growing, heavy water-using species are employed, and that planting forests on open land where the water table is close to the surface will lower groundwater levels [ev_water_yield_ham08_5, ev_water_yield_ham08_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_2]; after clearance, the streamflow gain declines as new cover establishes, and a return to pre-cut totals under natural regrowth may take more than eight years [ev_water_yield_ham08_8]. Planting programmes show the same: China's Grain-for-Green used mainly fast-growing non-native species that have reduced water supply [ev_water_yield_seddon21_10], and a cited New Zealand study notes afforestation reducing water yield while giving erosion benefits [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4]; a global review warns that large-scale afforestation in water-limited environments will inevitably exacerbate water scarcity [ev_water_yield_zhang17_7]. On the gain side, baseflow from Ethiopian catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]; a regional land-climate model projects significant increases of 11.4%, 16.9%, 17.6% and 84.9% in four regions under full reforestation potential [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_2, ev_water_regulation_teo22_3, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]; about 19 small watersheds and a large watershed showed increased annual runoff due to forest cover gain, and spruce reforestation of a Heihe River headwater was predicted to increase annual runoff by 8.6% for a 12.6% increase in forest cover [ev_water_yield_zhang17_5, ev_water_yield_zhang17_6]; and forest succession and declining evapotranspiration may explain increased summer streamflow at two temperate forest sites logged in the early nineteenth century [ev_water_yield_jon12_3].
conditionality: What separates the sides is baseline, method, species and time. The losses come from measured syntheses that pool forest restoration with other forms of forest cover expansion [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1], from reviews of reforestation and afforestation, and from planting with fast-growing or non-native species [ev_water_yield_ham08_6, ev_water_yield_seddon21_10]. The gains are an exclosure-versus-cropland contrast rather than a comparison with unrestored land [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], model projections at regional scale that work through precipitation as well as evapotranspiration [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_yield_zhang17_6], a minority of watersheds in a global review [ev_water_yield_zhang17_5], and a tentative attribution at sites logged in the early nineteenth century [ev_water_yield_jon12_3]. Some regions in the same model show nonsignificant declines where heightened evapotranspiration outstrips increases in precipitation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_5]. Several units are nulls: the global review failed to detect a statistically significant relationship between forest cover gain and annual runoff in small watersheds [ev_water_yield_zhang17_2], and an FAO–CIFOR review states that interception should put to rest the belief that extensive reforestation or afforestation will increase low flows in the dry season [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. Scale matters within the losses too: the decrease shrinks at larger temporal and spatial scales in the systematic review [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3], while the global review finds the runoff reduction significant only in large watersheds [ev_water_yield_zhang17_3]. The lowered water table under new forest is also described as improving drainage, so on waterlogged open land it is not purely a loss [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_2]. The class follows the sub-practice vote, replacing a pooled reading that had material weight on both sides. This row is for downstream users and basin planners: a loss here can coexist with local supply gains reported in the forest restoration water stress row, so read the two side by side rather than netting one against the other. Plantation results are reported in their own family row and do not count here.

effect_mechanism: A global systematic review pooling forest restoration with forestry and afforestation found that annual water yield decreased in about 80% of study cases reporting it and increased in 6% [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_1], baseflow decreased in 63% of cases [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2], groundwater levels or recharge decreased in 67% of the studies reporting them [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_filoso17_1], and no water-yield gains were observed in the meta-analysed subset [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3]. A global review of forest change found a significant negative relationship between forest cover gain and annual runoff in large watersheds, so the reduction is only significant there [ev_water_yield_zhang17_3]. Tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and much of the water that does soak in is used by the trees themselves [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, with groundwater recharge counted as a component, not whether the restored land itself holds more. Local supply sits in the water stress rows, and a loss here can coexist with a gain there, since the trees use much of the water that soaks in [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1]. The two syntheses read scale differently: in the systematic review the decrease shrinks at larger temporal and spatial scales [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_3], while the global review failed to detect a statistically significant relationship in small watersheds and found the reduction significant only in large ones [ev_water_yield_zhang17_2, ev_water_yield_zhang17_3]. The same global review records about 19 small watersheds and a large watershed with increased annual runoff due to forest cover gain, a minority reversal of the usual direction [ev_water_yield_zhang17_5]. Both reviews pool restoration with other forms of forest cover gain; the systematic review reports vote counts rather than pooled sizes, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies, and the baseflow cases are few [ev_water_regulation_filoso17_2].

effect_mechanism: In Ethiopia, catchments under exclosure pass more baseflow downstream than cropland does: baseflow from catchments with exclosures was 1.5 to 4 times greater than the baseflow from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]. At long-term research sites in the USA, forest succession and declining evapotranspiration may explain increased summer streamflow at two temperate forest sites logged in the early nineteenth century [ev_water_yield_jon12_3]. Against these, an FAO synthesis reports that after forest clearance the streamflow gain declines, irregularly, as the new cover establishes, and that a return to pre-cut streamflow totals in the case of natural regrowth may take more than eight years [ev_water_yield_ham08_8].
conditionality: What separates the sides is the starting point and the time scale. The FAO unit is about regrowth on freshly cleared land, where the gain in streamflow from cutting is used up again as the new cover grows [ev_water_yield_ham08_8]; it is harvest-recovery evidence, not a comparison with long-degraded land. The gains compare exclosures with cropland rather than with unrestored land, so that size is a contrast with farmed land, not a measured restoration gain [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and the US result is a tentative attribution at sites logged long ago, with no intervention described [ev_water_yield_jon12_3]. The positive class runs against the measured syntheses on forest cover expansion in the other catchment water yield rows; whether regeneration behaves differently from planting in this respect is suggested here, not shown. This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more.

effect_mechanism: Afforesting grasslands and shrublands reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and 31%, with proportionally larger reductions for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Cases in an FAO synthesis agree: the Fiji Pine Commission's planting of Caribbean Pinus in dry-zone grasslands resulted in dry-season streamflow reductions of 65 percent [ev_water_yield_ham08_7], and in South Africa, where nearly all plantations are on previously native grasslands, water reductions are in some cases experienced as soon as two years after planting, with maximum streamflow decreases relatively early in fast-growing stands [ev_water_yield_ham08_10]. A review of nature-based solutions adds that single-aged, low diversity, intensively managed plantations may reduce water availability in arid regions [ev_water_yield_seddon21_9].
conditionality: These are afforestation and plantation-forestry results, mostly from paired catchments and from grassland replaced by fast-growing exotic stands; the authors suggest the effects on water yield will be more severe in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_4], and in South Africa the maximum decreases occur early and then diminish [ev_water_yield_ham08_10]. Forest plantations of native tree species aged 25 to 45 years produce persistent dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to native old-growth forests, because of high water use by young, densely-spaced trees [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3]; that comparison is against old-growth forest rather than the land the plantation replaced, so it is held out of the class as a reference shortfall. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Forests use more water than the land cover that replaces them, so standing forest passes less water downstream: as both natural and human-established forests use more water than most replacement land cover, even partial forest removal increases downstream water yields [ev_water_yield_ham08_1], and replacing forest cover with other land uses almost always results in increased runoff and streamflow [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_2]. All of almost 100 paired catchment experiments involving removal of forest cover gave higher streamflow totals [ev_water_yield_ham08_4]; first-year increases after clearance in the humid tropics range from 110 to 825 mm depending on local rainfall [ev_water_yield_ham08_3], the greatest percentage increase falls in the dry season [ev_water_yield_ham08_2], and daily late-summer flows rose by up to 300% after experimental harvest, though most daily changes were 50% or less [ev_water_yield_jon12_2]. Global syntheses agree: more forest cover loss tends to increase annual runoff in both large and small watersheds [ev_water_yield_zhang17_1], an increase in forest coverage reduces the share of rainfall leaving as runoff [ev_water_yield_zhou15_1], and changes to forests in water-limited watersheds can lead to larger water-yield responses [ev_water_yield_zhou15_2]. Harvesting or removing forest also raises groundwater levels [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_1].
conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more, and it can coexist with the local gains recorded in the protection water stress row. Every unit compares existing forest with its harvest, clearance or loss, which is why the row sits in the protection family and not in the forest restoration roll-up; none measures the outcome of a protection or community forest management project. Two measured results run the other way: very small summer events decreased by more than 40% in the first 2 years after canopy removal in the Fox Creek basins [ev_water_yield_jon00_1], and 25 to 35 years after harvest, summer streamflow in regenerating temperate basins declined by up to 30%-50% relative to uncut reference basins [ev_water_yield_jon12_1] - the regrowth result is restoration-direction evidence that young regenerating forest can draw summer flow below what old forest yields. The null stays named: 12 (of 61) large and 33 (of 252) small watersheds showed no significant change in annual runoff despite forest cover loss [ev_water_yield_zhang17_4]. The groundwater statement also cuts both ways: planting forests on open land where the water table is close to the surface will lower groundwater levels, improving drainage, while removal can move soil salts into the rooting zone [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_1].

effect_mechanism: Cost per hectare depends mainly on method: modelled implementation cost has a median of US$140/ha for natural regeneration [ev_project_cost_busch24_1], natural regeneration methods are cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects in the tropics and subtropics [ev_project_cost_williams24_2], and natural regeneration in Uganda is tabled at US$26/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_5]. A Brazilian cost survey reports the same gap: direct seeding and seedling planting cost approximately ten times more (about US$2000/ha) than natural and assisted regeneration and enrichment planting (about US$200/ha), mostly due to the higher input costs [ev_project_cost_branc19_1, ev_project_cost_branc19_2, ev_project_cost_branc19_3]. The opportunity cost of land (median US$4,807/ha) is generally higher and more variable than implementation cost [ev_project_cost_busch24_5].
conditionality: Most reported figures state no price year, some are assumptions rather than observed costs [ev_project_cost_wri17_1], and WOCAT values are compiler-entered conversions from local currency. Values from high-income and upper-middle-income settings, including the Brazilian survey figures, are excluded from the low and lower-middle income range. Plantation results are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

justification.mechanism: In a plantation trial on pasture in La Chontalpa, Tabasco, Mexico, semi-mechanised planting cost US$178/ha against US$217/ha by hand [ev_project_cost_keyes97_1, ev_project_cost_keyes97_2]; plantation establishment in the Masoala corridors of Madagascar is listed at 279 dollars per hectare [ev_project_cost_wri17_3]; and modelled implementation cost for plantations across low- and middle-income countries has a median of US$3,729/ha, inclusive of replanting after harvest cycles, against US$140/ha for natural regeneration [ev_project_cost_busch24_2].
justification.conditionality: The cost class is set by the Madagascar entry, the only one in the low-income band; the Mexican and modelled figures sit outside it. The Mexican figures are historical field costs for establishment and first-year maintenance that exclude donated seedlings, and the modelled median counts replanting over harvest cycles, with an interdecile range of US$1,530–11,675/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation costs, not the cost of restoration toward a natural baseline. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: Abatement cost compares implementation and land opportunity costs with the carbon gained: modelled natural regeneration costs a median of US$23.80 per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_busch24_3]. In Colombia's western Andes a median carbon price of US$1.99 per tCO2 over 30 years was enough to compensate landowners for letting pastures regenerate [ev_project_cost_chazdon16_1], and conserving 90% of remaining mangroves could be achieved at carbon prices between 3.0 and 13.0 US$ per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2]. Two payment schemes report low programme costs per tonne of carbon: the PAS scheme in Brazil was estimated at 0.56 USD per ton of CO2, and the Ugandan scheme cost $0.57 per ton of delayed emissions against an estimated social benefit of $1.11 per ton, roughly two times the cost [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3].
conditionality: All units are modelled or break-even prices rather than project budgets, and the mangrove conservation figure concerns avoided emissions from protecting existing forest rather than restoration; the Colombian figure is cited from another study and states no price year. The Brazilian figure is a total programme cost given without assessing cost-effectiveness, both payment figures are cited in a systematic review, and both concern paying landholders to keep existing forest rather than restoring it [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3]. Plantation results are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

effect_mechanism: Natural regeneration lowers cost by letting forests grow back on their own or with low-cost assistance, cited at US$12-3,880/ha against US$105-25,830/ha for restoration projects, and is often more effective than full tree planting in long-term success [ev_project_cost_williams24_1]; European guidelines likewise note its lower cost and locally adapted genetic material [ev_project_cost_stanturf26_1]. In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. Decentralised administration of Van Panchayat forests in India is associated with costs approximately 1/13th of those under state administration [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].
conditionality: The European statement is an expert assertion that also notes limits in species composition, and the cost comparison is a cited range without price year. Organic mulches cut cost per established plant less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter, and the result comes from a single experiment at one site [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]; the Van Panchayat cost figure is cited in a systematic review and concerns administering existing forest [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].

effect_mechanism: Reforestation slows storm runoff and lowers flood peaks in catchment models: in Slovakia's Hornad watershed a 50% increase of forest cut a simulated flood peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and reduced peaks by about 24% on average in rain-duration tests, more for short storms than long ones [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and an afforestation simulation for Luxembourg's Alzette basin decreased the peak by 8% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. A systematic review found that flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of studies reporting them [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]. In a US experimental basin the gradual recovery of peak discharges over time after clear-cutting, as vegetation regrew, is attributed to changes in evapotranspiration [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_5]. An FAO synthesis accepts that locally, for frequent short, low-intensity storm events, flash flooding should be reduced where soils are deep [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_7], and a cited synthesis expects afforestation in energy-limited environments to help reduce flood risks [ev_flood_hazard_zhang17_1]. WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan and a learning site in Afghanistan rate downstream flooding or flood impacts as reduced; an Ethiopian compiler notes that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced, and the Afghan compiler that riverbanks were revegetated with communities planting cuttings along banks and shorelines [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
conditionality: The benefit is off-site for farmers: it lands on downstream flood exposure, not on the restored plot. It is also scale- and storm-bound. The same FAO synthesis that accepts the local effect calls it a misperception that reforesting watersheds reduces or prevents floods, with no evidence for this except at the very local scale of a few hundred hectares [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_5, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_6]. Himalayan position papers reach the same null: estimated peak rainfall intensities balanced against soil infiltration capacities lead to the conclusion that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on local flooding, and certainly not on the Ganges and Brahmaputra mainstreams [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_1], and reforestation in the mountains conceived as a palliative for the plains is likely to reap only disappointment [ev_flood_hazard_ivesmt87_1]. An FAO–CIFOR review concludes that massive programmes of forestation proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may have many other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a comment on a global flood analysis argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding, for example if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change, and settlements, roads and drains remain unaltered [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. These nulls are expert positions rather than measurements. The modelled benefit shrinks as rain continues, from 29% for the shortest rain duration to 17% for the longest [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and all catchment results are scenarios of large forest-cover gains in temperate high-income basins; the largest figure, a 42.3% peak reduction from converting all arable land to forest, is a secondary citation with no basin named [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The Honduras compiler rates no downstream change yet, expecting reforestation to reduce floods in the lower river only in the long term, and the Bosnia and Herzegovina compiler rates only a slight reduction [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_downstream_flooding]. The review pools restoration with forestry and afforestation and reports vote counts rather than magnitudes [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1], and the low- and middle-income evidence consists of WOCAT compiler ratings, not measured flows or flood damage. effect_mechanism: Catchment models find that adding forest lowers flood peaks: a reforestation scenario in Slovakia's Hornad basin cut simulated peak discharge by 12% for one flood and by 18% on average over the simulation period, with reductions of 29% for the shortest storms and 17% for the longest, and a cited afforestation simulation in Luxembourg gives 8% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_2, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. conditionality: All units come from high-income temperate settings. The catchment results are models of large forest increases whose effect becomes less as rain continues for longer [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3], and the US result tracks a basin recovering from clear-cutting rather than a restoration project, so it shows that regrowth brings peaks back down without saying how much or from what practice [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_5]. justification.mechanism: Adding forest to a catchment lowers flood peaks in models: in the Hornad watershed of Slovakia a reforestation scenario cut the simulated peak discharge by 12%, by 18% on average over the simulation period and by about 24% on average for synthetic storms, and a cited Alzette basin study in Luxembourg found an 8% reduction [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_2, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. An FAO synthesis accepts that locally, for frequent short, low-intensity storm events, flash flooding should be reduced where soils are deep [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_7], and a cited synthesis expects afforestation in energy-limited environments to help reduce flood risks [ev_flood_hazard_zhang17_1]. WOCAT compilers rate flood impacts as reduced for Tugai floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan and for afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_flood_impacts].
justification.conditionality: The flood benefit is off-site for farmers and local in scale. The same FAO synthesis finds no evidence that reforesting watersheds reduces or prevents floods except at the very local scale of a few hundred hectares [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_5, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_6]; Himalayan position papers judge that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on local flooding, and certainly not on the Ganges and Brahmaputra mainstreams [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_1], and that mountain reforestation as a palliative for the plains is likely to reap only disappointment [ev_flood_hazard_ivesmt87_1]. These nulls are expert positions, not measurements. The modelled effect shrinks for long storms (29% for the shortest rain duration, 17% for the longest) and the quantified evidence comes from models of large land-cover changes in high-income temperate basins, well beyond project scale [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3]; the largest figure, 42.3% from converting all arable land to forest, is a secondary citation [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The Honduras compiler rates no effect yet, expecting flood reduction only in the long term [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding], and the low-income evidence is practitioner ratings, the Eritrea sheet combining planting with hillside terracing. The Uganda tree-planting rating has moved to the plantation family's flood row.

effect_mechanism: Flooding or peak flows decreased with forest cover expansion in 82% of the studies with data on them in a global systematic review, consistent with forest cover slowing storm runoff [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1], and in a US experimental basin the gradual recovery of peak discharges after clear-cutting, as vegetation regrew, is attributed to changes in evapotranspiration [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_5].
conditionality: The review pools explicit and implicit forest restoration with forestry and afforestation, is dominated by temperate and Oceania studies, and reports vote counts rather than effect sizes, so it does not say how large the reduction is or which restoration practice delivers it [ev_flood_hazard_filoso17_1]; the US result is regrowth after a clear-cut, not a restoration project, and does not name a practice [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_5]. No unit comes from a low- or lower-middle-income setting. Expert positions point the other way: an FAO–CIFOR synthesis concludes that massive forestation programmes proclaimed as the answer to preventing floods simply will not do the job, although reforestation may bring other benefits [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_3], and a published comment argues that reforestation does not necessarily reduce flooding if soil properties do not recover, river bed morphology does not change and settlements, roads and drains remain [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_5]. Neither is a measurement. Any benefit is off-site for farmers.

effect_mechanism: This row describes the flood regulation that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. It is well established that partial or complete removal of tree cover accelerates water discharge, increasing the risk of flood during the rainy season [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_1], and for frequent rainfall events of short duration or low intensity, forested soils may reduce or prevent flash floods locally [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_3]; forests and forest soils reduce runoff through enhanced infiltration and storage, and peak flows rise after forest removal in small experimental catchments [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_2]. Paired-basin experiments in the USA measure the cost of harvest: forest harvesting increased peak discharges by as much as 50% in small basins and 100% in large basins over 50 years, attributable to roads and to water-balance changes [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_1]; in small basins discharges rose by 50% in the first 5 years and stayed 25 to 40% above pretreatment up to 25 years later [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_2, ev_flood_hazard_jg96_3]; and in 100%-clear-cut basins large events increased by 25%, 16% and 26% at Andrews 1, Andrews 6 and Coyote 3 [ev_flood_hazard_jon00_1]. A country-level analysis of developing countries predicted that a further hypothetical 10% loss of natural forest cover would raise flood frequency by 3.5% to 28.1% and flood duration by 3.8% to 7.9% [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_1, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_2]; in Malaysia an analysis with adequate controls for confounding factors found flood risk increased after natural forest was converted to plantation crops and urban land [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_1], and in Swiss valleys with more than 30% forest snowmelt was more gradual and flooding risk lower [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_2]. At a learning site in Afghanistan the compiler rates flood impacts as decreased after riverbanks were revegetated through control measures [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
conditionality: The service fades with storm size and basin size. For the rarer prolonged or high-intensity storms, once the soil layer becomes saturated, water runs off even under full, undisturbed forest cover [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_4]; forest soils reduce runoff only in small-scale rainfall events, which are not responsible for severe downstream flooding, and forests cannot stop catastrophic large-scale floods caused by severe meteorological events [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_2]; small to medium peak flows are affected most while the largest events do not change noticeably, and studies in larger basins have not usually found changes after deforestation of up to 50% of the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_3, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_4]. The harvest experiments carry their own nulls: complete clear-cutting without roads raised fall and winter events but not large events as a group [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_4], large events did not change at Andrews 10 [ev_flood_hazard_jon00_2], and the large-basin increases are bundled with forest road construction, so they cannot be credited to forest cover alone [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_1]. A worldwide review found no cause and effect demonstrated between forest cutting in the headwaters and floods in the lower basin, with no conflicting information published more than 20 years later [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_2], and on the Himalayan scale human influences on plains flooding are contended to be insignificant so far [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_2]. The cross-country analysis itself found little evidence that further forest loss changed flood deaths or damage [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_3, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_4], and a reanalysis of its data found the correlation between forest cover or cover loss and flood frequency appears absent, with the degraded-lands fraction accounting for most of the variation [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_1]. Every unit except the Afghanistan rating compares forest with cleared or less-forested land, so the row shows what losing forest costs rather than the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme; that is why these units sit in the protection family and not in the restoration roll-up. The Afghanistan unit is a practitioner rating from a learning site that bundles several land and forest management practices [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts]. Benefits fall downstream, off-site for farmers.

effect_mechanism: A global remote-sensing comparison of forest-cover change found that forest gain cooled annual land surface temperature by 0.18 degrees C in tropical and 0.19 degrees C in temperate regions, and by 1.11 degrees C where tropical forest cover rose by about 50%, consistent with tree cover buffering local temperature [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_1, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_2, ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_4].
conditionality: Forestation had null effects in boreal regions [ev_microclimate_buffering_prevedello19_3]. The study tracks observed forest-cover gain, not a named planting or regeneration practice, and measures annual land surface temperature rather than heat stress on crops, livestock or people; all units come from a single source.

effect_mechanism: Across restoration families the gain runs mostly through fodder and livestock: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, India, Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan rate fodder and animal production as increased, from cut-and-carry grass in enclosures, planted sand-fixing species used as forage and better grazing management. Crop gains are reported where regeneration improves soils or supplies mulch, and in Niger assisted natural regeneration in fields is reported to raise millet and sorghum output by almost 50%; in Brazil the Reflorestar payments-for-ecosystem-services programme raised agricultural value added and production value in the poorest municipalities. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and one Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged; much of the evidence is fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield. The Brazilian quasi-experimental gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state, and the source reports a heterogeneous, negative response in better-off municipalities. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

justification.mechanism: Across restoration families the gain runs mostly through fodder and livestock: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, India, Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan rate fodder and animal production as increased, from cut-and-carry grass in enclosures, planted sand-fixing species used as forage and better grazing management. Crop gains are reported where regeneration improves soils or supplies mulch, and in Niger assisted natural regeneration in fields is reported to raise millet and sorghum output by almost 50%; in Brazil the Reflorestar payments-for-ecosystem-services programme raised agricultural value added and production value in the poorest municipalities. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
justification.conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and one Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged; much of the evidence is fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield. The Brazilian quasi-experimental gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state, and the source reports a heterogeneous, negative response in better-off municipalities. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

conditionality: Every unit is a compiler rating rather than a measured yield, fodder is a component proxy for the production gap, and no unit reports crop yields; the Eritrea sheet combines planting with hillside terracing.

effect_mechanism: Recurrent costs are annual maintenance costs per hectare entered on WOCAT sheets for regeneration, community forest and other restoration technologies in Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan, Honduras and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance], plus a WRI table entry for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
conditionality: Values span a very wide range because the technologies and cost items differ, the WOCAT figures are compiler entries mostly converted from local currency, and the WRI figure has no price year [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]; the units from upper-middle-income countries were set aside from the class, which rests on the low- and lower-middle-income entries. The Costa Rican figure is a payment for keeping forest, expressed per hectare of forest that would not otherwise have been there, and is cited in a systematic review rather than drawn from programme accounts [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
