justification.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs per hectare on WOCAT sheets for the community forest package in India and the protected learning site in Afghanistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
justification.conditionality: The two compiler entries differ widely, the Indian one is converted from local currency and spread over mixed plantation and nursery areas, and neither sheet itemises maintenance tasks [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance]. The Costa Rican figure is payment spending per hectare of additional forest rather than a maintenance cost, from an upper-middle-income country, and is cited in a systematic review [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].

effect_mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases (the underlying global review of community forest management counts 316 such cases) [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1], community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Even the global community-forest review behind the 68% figure records 26% of cases with no change in incomes and 6.3% with decreases, and it pools community with household income [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group. Plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations, Costa Rican payments for reforestation plantings and modelled plantation profitability, are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

effect_mechanism: In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains for participants, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. In Guanacaste, Costa Rica, payments for environmental services under the reforestation modality made up 18.66% of participants' income during the contract, covered a substantial part of the costs of establishing and maintaining the plantation, and brought family employment and legal security over the property [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]; similar Latin American programmes reach around 10% of family income [ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Modelled plantations would be profitable even without carbon payments across 28.3% of the area feasible for them [ev_economic_return_busch24_1], and compilers for afforestation in Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns as very positive, the Uzbek compiler noting that unprofitable land would start bringing benefit [ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income].
conditionality: These are production-plantation results: smallholder plantations, commercial plantations under a payment scheme, and modelled plantations with harvest. The Vietnam return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and the gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1], the Costa Rica evidence comes from a high-income setting, and the Uganda compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are compiler ratings or modelled, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand and, in large studies controlling for socio-economic factors, drove poverty reduction [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1]: a meta-analysis of counterfactual studies finds small positive effects of protected areas on local monetary outcomes (g = 0.028) and poverty outcomes (g = 0.117) [ev_household_income_kandel22_1, ev_rural_poverty_kandel22_1], households in the Chitwan National Park buffer zone of Nepal have 19 percent higher per capita income [ev_household_income_kandel22_2], and across developing countries living within 10 km of protected areas with documented tourism lowers the likelihood of poverty by 16.1% and of child stunting by 13.4%, with poverty 8.8% lower near multiple-use protected areas even without tourism [ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_1, ev_food_security_naidoo19_1, ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_2]. effect_mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes, and the sub-practice rows agree on that direction. In the passive regeneration evidence, an Ethiopian meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, an Ethiopian compiler noting an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years and less sediment transported [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss]; the higher probability of landslides after timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. The planting evidence carries the measured and modelled magnitudes: in Pakistan a watershed restoration of tree planting, grazing control and erosion control structures reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed land [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2], tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2], vegetation restoration in China could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1], and targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]. FAO syntheses call forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded cleared land, and in Taiwan a rehabilitation programme reduced reservoir sedimentation by 55 percent of the base rate [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. Community-managed sites add compiler ratings: the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands, the Afghanistan compiler rates surface runoff decreased, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. Assisted natural regeneration compilers in Niger and Bangladesh rate soil loss decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss].
conditionality: The benefit is largely off-site for farmers: much of it is reduced runoff and sediment reaching downstream land and channels rather than better soil on their own plots [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Nulls and dissent stay named. In China the soil conservation measures, including vegetation and engineering, contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and on the Loess Plateau an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover was attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1], young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support of its older predecessors [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides, an Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation], and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The largest measured reductions are bundles: the Pakistan results combine planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, check dams and other structures, and the Taiwan programme combines reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, so none can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. Many units are WOCAT compiler ratings, several sheets bundle closure or planting with structures such as bunds [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation], afforestation in New Zealand reduces erosion at the cost of water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], and the runoff results measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Studies of what existing forest does, including logging and harvest landslide studies, sit in the protection family row and do not count here, and plantation results are kept in their own family row, out of this roll-up.

justification.mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes, and the sub-practice rows agree on that direction. In the passive regeneration evidence, an Ethiopian meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, an Ethiopian compiler noting an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years and less sediment transported [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss]; the higher probability of landslides after timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. The planting evidence carries the measured and modelled magnitudes: in Pakistan a watershed restoration of tree planting, grazing control and erosion control structures reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed land [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2], tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2], vegetation restoration in China could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1], and targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]. FAO syntheses call forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded cleared land, and in Taiwan a rehabilitation programme reduced reservoir sedimentation by 55 percent of the base rate [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. Community-managed sites add compiler ratings: the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands, the Afghanistan compiler rates surface runoff decreased, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. Assisted natural regeneration compilers in Niger and Bangladesh rate soil loss decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss].
justification.conditionality: The benefit is largely off-site for farmers: much of it is reduced runoff and sediment reaching downstream land and channels rather than better soil on their own plots [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Nulls and dissent stay named. In China the soil conservation measures, including vegetation and engineering, contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and on the Loess Plateau an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover was attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1], young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support of its older predecessors [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides, an Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation], and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The largest measured reductions are bundles: the Pakistan results combine planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, check dams and other structures, and the Taiwan programme combines reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, so none can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. Many units are WOCAT compiler ratings, several sheets bundle closure or planting with structures such as bunds [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation], afforestation in New Zealand reduces erosion at the cost of water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], and the runoff results measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Studies of what existing forest does, including logging and harvest landslide studies, sit in the protection family row and do not count here, and plantation results are kept in their own family row, out of this roll-up.

effect_mechanism: In high-income settings tree cover reduces erosion through slope reinforcement and slower runoff: reforestation of just 9.3 percent (159 km2) of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment could decrease total landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]; afforestation in New Zealand provides erosion reduction benefits [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]; reforestation in Slovakia's Hornad watershed is modelled to decrease surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]; and in Taiwan reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2].
conditionality: The New Zealand afforestation benefit comes with reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], the Waipaoa and Hornad results are model scenarios [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1], and the Taiwan reduction is credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, cited in an FAO review [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. A US observation runs the other way on slopes: young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support that its much larger and older predecessors did [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5]. The row applies only to high-income contexts and does not transfer directly to low-income settings. Plantation results are kept in their own family rows, out of forest restoration.

effect_mechanism: Planted cover reduces runoff and soil loss on the restored slope and catchment, so the benefit reaches farmers off-site, through less sediment and runoff arriving downslope and downstream rather than on the plot itself. In Pakistan a watershed restoration of tree planting, control of grazing and erosion control structures reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], and Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed areas with natural vegetation [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2]. A review of Chinese vegetation restoration finds it could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once vegetation cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. A model of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment finds that reforesting just 9.3% of it could cut sediment inputs from landslides by about 20% [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6], a Slovak catchment model shows reforestation decreasing surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1], and in Ethiopia tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff depth from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. WOCAT compilers in Eritrea, Cabo Verde, Tajikistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate soil loss as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1523_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_soil_loss], with surface runoff and downstream siltation also rated as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1330_2010_surface_runoff, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4367_2019_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_siltation].
conditionality: The Pakistan results are bundles - planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, check dams and spillways - so the reduction cannot be credited to planting alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2]. The Chinese evidence carries its own nulls: in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area vegetation and engineering measures together contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures in the past 20 years [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and a four-year measurement in 12 small Loess Plateau watersheds found an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover and attributed it to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1]. In New Zealand erosion benefits trade off against reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]. The Waipaoa result is modelled and is landslide sediment recorded under erosion for lack of a landslide category, runoff and sediment enter as components, and the low-income evidence is compiler ratings apart from the Ethiopian runoff measurements [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Plantation results, including the warnings that dense planted monocultures without understorey or litter can raise erosion, sit in the plantation family's erosion row, out of this row and the roll-up.

effect_mechanism: Review statements that name restoration generically, not a single family, sit here. An FAO regional review of forests and landslides in Asia asserts that tree planting on susceptible slopes can reduce risk, and that natural regeneration and tree planting on failed slopes can help control after-effects such as sediment release into rivers [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_1]. An FAO forests-and-water synthesis calls forest restoration one of the best ways of restoring productivity and reducing sedimentation in degraded areas of cleared land experiencing accelerated erosion [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1], and lists reducing soil loss and keeping sediment out of streams among the very good reasons for rehabilitating watersheds [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_1]. It cites Taiwan, where reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The effect is off-site for farmers: stabilised slopes and less sediment reaching rivers and reservoirs, at slope and catchment scale rather than on the farm plot.
conditionality: Only the Taiwan unit says how large the effect is, which is why the class is capped; the other statements are FAO assertions without a measured value. The Taiwan reduction is credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control, check dams and gully control, fruit trees and agroforestry, and conservation farming, so it cannot be attributed to forest restoration alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The same synthesis is explicit that achieving substantial flood reduction is not among the reasons to rehabilitate watersheds [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_1]. No unit comes from a low- or lower-middle-income setting. The primary landslide and watershed studies behind the Asia review are now registered in their own rows (passive regeneration, active planting and protection). Landslide risk is recorded under erosion here for lack of a landslide category.

On harvested slopes, the higher probability of landslides following timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2], and a global forest-water assessment adds that land abandonment with expanding forest and grassland has in some cases decreased soil erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_5].
justification.conditionality: The same global assessment reports that abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes is particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4], and one Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation]. Regrowth is slow to restore slope protection: young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support that its much larger and older predecessors did [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], and the landslide recovery result tracks regrowth after timber harvest, not a restoration project, without separating replanting from natural regeneration [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. Apart from these reviews and the Ethiopian meta-analysis, which measures runoff as a component of erosion, the units are compiler ratings, and some regeneration sheets combine enclosure with physical structures such as bunds, so the share due to regrowth alone is not isolated [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as less runoff and sediment downstream.

effect_mechanism: Under good tree cover erosion falls: in eucalyptus afforestation in Calabria, Italy, sediment concentrations were substantially greater on a plot with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1], and the Uganda afforestation compiler rates soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1577_2013_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation]. Erosion can still worsen, and this is reported as harm rather than averaged away: particularly serious erosion problems arise in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], and an FAO synthesis names dense, planted monocultures with little or no understorey and ground cover as experiencing increased surface erosion rates [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4].
conditionality: Gains and losses both carry material weight, so no direction is stated. What separates them is the ground layer under the trees: the gains come where canopy and cover are good, the losses where understorey, vegetation and litter are absent, cleared or collected [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4]. The actionable reading is a management condition, keeping understorey and litter, rather than a property of plantations as such. Both loss statements come from syntheses rather than measurements and state no comparator; the gain side is a high-income Italian catchment study plus compiler ratings from Uganda. An earlier cited statement on throughfall energy under plantations without understorey was rejected at review for lacking a valid comparator and is not counted. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

effect_mechanism: This row describes the soil and slope protection that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Forest cover provides the most effective barrier to natural erosion, and loss of forest cover to other land uses always increases human-accelerated erosion unless soil conservation is carried out [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]; in the Ethiopian highlands soil loss under forest averaged 1 tonne per hectare, the lowest of seven categories of land use [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_3]. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: in a US study area the number and acreage of slides increased four and one-half or more times after logging began in 1953, and the scarcity of slides on timbered slopes near logged areas strongly indicates increased susceptibility from logging [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_2]; investigations in steep forested terrain worldwide note up to a 10-fold increase in landslide erosion roughly 3–15 yr after timber harvesting, and rates of mass erosion can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after harvest [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]; mean suspended sediment at managed Sabah catchments was several times higher in the most affected period after logging than before it [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_3]; and in Japan most landslides happened in young forest stands, shrublands and grasslands, the preventive function of the forest increasing with its age class [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_4]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil mechanical support [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]; root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. Nulls stay named: in Thailand landslide density appeared independent of vegetation cover, the storm magnitude overwhelming the stabilising influence of root strength [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_4]; a cited study found lumbering had no part in contributing to slide occurrence and suspected forest maturity of slightly raising slide probability [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_3]; and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The logging, harvest and land-use comparisons are evidence about what existing forest does and what its loss costs, not the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme, which is why they sit in this family and not in the restoration roll-up [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as fewer slides and less sediment downslope and downstream.

effect_mechanism: Lower sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on. WOCAT compilers for planting, regeneration and protection technologies in Ethiopia, Tanzania, Cape Verde, India and Bangladesh rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, sediment deposited behind bunds, improved vegetation cover and controlled erosion, and slower sediment and runoff [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO forests-and-water synthesis calls forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded areas of cleared land experiencing accelerated erosion [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1], and cites Taiwan, where reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2].
conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation]. Apart from the FAO synthesis, the units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data such as nutrients or turbidity, and some sheets combine vegetation with physical structures such as bunds. The Taiwan reduction is a high-income case credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control, check dams, agroforestry and conservation farming, so it cannot be attributed to forest restoration alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The benefit falls off-site for farmers, on downstream water users and reservoirs.

effect_mechanism: WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate water quantity, availability and harvesting or collection as improved: the Indian compiler cites better soil water-holding capacity from slower runoff and improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, and the Afghan compiler cites water seeping into the ground through revegetation and improved land cover, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water]. US paired-basin experiments show what standing forest does to peak flows: forest canopy removal accounted for significant increases (31–116%) in peak discharges during the first postharvest decade in 8 of 10 treated basins, though the affected events were small and fell in the fall when soils are in moisture deficit [ev_water_regulation_jon00_1], and changes in snowpack dynamics accounted for significant increases (25–31%) in winter rain-on-snow events [ev_water_regulation_jon00_6].
conditionality: The compiler units come from sheets that bundle several practices — broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, a learning site for sustainable land and forest management in Afghanistan — with no measured flow or groundwater data, so the gain cannot be credited to protection alone. The US units are harvest experiments: evidence about what existing forest does, not the result of a protection programme, which is why they sit in this family and not in the roll-up; they measure peak discharge, a regulation component, rather than water available to users [ev_water_regulation_jon00_1]. They carry their own nulls: other types of winter events did not change [ev_water_regulation_jon00_7], and changes in cloud water interception apparently offset changes in evapotranspiration in two partially cut basins [ev_water_regulation_jon00_5]. Whether keeping forest standing changes the water passed downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.
